channel.title: Wire — Releases
channel.description: Releases from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: AWS Batch now supports Amazon ECS Managed Instances
item.description: AWS Batch now supports Amazon ECS Managed Instances (ECS MI) as a new compute option, enabling you to run GPU-accelerated and compute-intensive batch workloads on AWS-managed infrastructure. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Capacity Reservation Resource Groups now support Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks and interruptible Capacity Reservations
item.description: Starting today, you can add Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible Capacity Reservations to Capacity Reservation Resource Groups. (1 source: aws)

item.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports AWS PrivateLink
item.description: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports AWS PrivateLink, enabling private connectivity to Lambda MicroVMs directly from Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) resources without exposing traffic to the public internet. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you update the customer profile on a case or add a profile after a case is opened
item.description: Amazon Connect Customer now lets agents change the profile on a case or choose a profile after the case is opened. If a case is linked to the wrong customer, agents can update the profile to keep case histories accurate. (1 source: aws)

item.title: AWS IoT Core now supports native InfluxDB routing for time-series data
item.description: AWS IoT Core now supports InfluxDB rule action that routes time-series data from your Internet of Things (IoT) devices directly to InfluxDB databases, without writing custom device-side code or using intermediate cloud services. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL supports minor versions 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24
item.description: Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL now supports the latest minor versions 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24. (1 source: aws)
